title.zh: 卷一百二十六 載記第二十六 禿髮烏孤 禿髮利鹿孤 禿髮傉檀
title.en: Volume 126 Records 26: Tufa Wugu; Tufa Lilugu; Tufa Rutan
title.raw: 卷一百二十六 載記第二十六 禿髮烏孤 禿髮利鹿孤 禿髮傉檀 Volume 126 Records 26: Tufa Wugu; Tufa Lilugu; Tufa Rutan

sentences.zh: 禿髮烏孤

translations.literal: Tufa Wugu
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Wugu

sentences.zh: 禿髮烏孤，河西鮮卑人也。

translations.literal: Tufa Wugu was a Xianbei of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Wugu was a Xianbei chieftain of the Hexi corridor.

sentences.zh: 其先與後魏同出。

translations.literal: His ancestors came forth together with Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His line had sprung from the same stock as Later Wei.

sentences.zh: 八世祖匹孤率其部自塞北遷於河西，其地東至麥田、牽屯，西至濕羅，南至澆河，北接大漠。

translations.literal: His eighth-generation ancestor Pigu led his tribe from beyond the frontier north into Hexi; their lands extended east to Maitian and Qiantun, west to Shiruo, south to the Jiao River, and north to the great desert.
translations.idiomatic: Eight generations back, Pigu had led the tribe from the northern marches into Hexi, holding a domain that ran east to Maitian and Qiantun, west to Shiruo, south to the Jiao River, and north to the edge of the great desert.

sentences.zh: 匹孤卒，子壽闐立。

translations.literal: When Pigu died, his son Shoutian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Pigu died and was succeeded by his son Shoutian.

sentences.zh: 初，壽闐之在孕，母胡掖氏因寢而產於被中，鮮卑謂被為「禿髮」，因而氏焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Shoutian was still in the womb, his mother Lady Hu She gave birth to him in the bedding; the Xianbei word for bedding is tufa, and from that they took their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Shoutian's mother, Lady Hu She, had borne him in the bedding while he was still in the womb; in Xianbei a quilt was called tufa, and from that word the clan took its name.

sentences.zh: 壽闐卒，孫樹機能立，壯果多謀略。

translations.literal: When Shoutian died, his grandson Shunengji succeeded; he was strong, resolute, and full of stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: After Shoutian's death his grandson Shunengji came to power—a man of force, daring, and many stratagems.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，殺秦州刺史胡烈于萬斛堆，敗涼州刺史蘇愉于金山，盡有涼州之地，武帝為之旰食。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era he killed Qinzhou Inspector Hu Lie at Wandui heap, defeated Liangzhou Inspector Su Yu at Jinshan, and held all of Liangzhou; Emperor Wu lost sleep over it.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taishi period he killed Qinzhou inspector Hu Lie at Wandui Mound, routed Liangzhou inspector Su Yu at Jinshan, and seized all of Liangzhou—so that Emperor Wu of Jin could scarcely eat for worry.

sentences.zh: 後為馬隆所敗，部下殺之以降。

translations.literal: Later he was defeated by Ma Long; his followers killed him and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Long later defeated him, and his own men slew him and submitted.

sentences.zh: 從弟務丸立。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Wuwan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Wuwan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 死，孫推斤立。

translations.literal: He died, and his grandson Tuojin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his grandson Tuojin took the leadership.

sentences.zh: 死，子思復鞬立，部眾稍盛。

translations.literal: He died, and his son Sifujian succeeded; the following grew somewhat stronger.
translations.idiomatic: He died in turn, and his son Sifujian succeeded, by which time the tribe had grown somewhat stronger.

sentences.zh: 烏孤即思復鞬之子也。

translations.literal: Wugu was the son of Sifujian.
translations.idiomatic: Wugu was Sifujian's son.

sentences.zh: 及嗣位，務農桑，修鄰好。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to rule, he promoted agriculture and sericulture and cultivated good relations with neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: On succeeding, he encouraged farming and sericulture and kept friendly ties with neighboring powers.

sentences.zh: 呂光遣使署為假節、冠軍大將軍、河西鮮卑大都統、廣武縣侯。

translations.literal: Lü Guang sent envoys to appoint him acting commissioner, Grand General Who Conquers the Champions, Grand Commander of the Hexi Xianbei, and Marquis of Guangwu County.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang dispatched envoys to invest him as acting commissioner, Grand General Who Conquers the Champions, supreme commander of the Hexi Xianbei, and Marquis of Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 烏孤謂諸將曰：「呂氏遠來假授，當可受不？

translations.literal: Wugu said to his generals, "The Lü clan has come from afar to grant us titles at their pleasure—ought we accept?"
translations.idiomatic: Wugu asked his commanders, "The Lü have sent titles from far away—should we take them?"

sentences.zh: 」眾咸曰：「吾士眾不少，何故屬人！

translations.literal: All said, "Our warriors are not few—why submit to another!"
translations.idiomatic: They all cried, "Our warriors are numerous enough—why bow to anyone else!"

sentences.zh: 」烏孤將從之，其將石真若留曰：「今本根未固，理宜隨時。

translations.literal: Wugu was about to agree when his officer Shizhen Ruoliu said, "Our roots are not yet firm; by reason we should follow the times."
translations.idiomatic: Wugu was on the point of agreeing when his officer Shizhen Ruoliu said, "Our foundations are still weak; it is only sensible to bend with the moment."

sentences.zh: 光德刑修明，境內無虞，若致死於我者，大小不敵，後雖悔之，無所及也。

translations.literal: Guang's virtue and punishments are well ordered, and within his borders there is no trouble; if we bring death on ourselves, great and small are not matched, and though we regret it later there will be no remedy."
translations.idiomatic: "Guang's laws are clear and his realm is at peace. If we defy him to our ruin, we cannot match his strength; when regret comes, nothing can undo it."

sentences.zh: 不如受而遵養之，又待其釁耳。

translations.literal: Better to accept and nurture compliance, and wait for his lapse besides."
translations.idiomatic: "Better to accept, keep ourselves in his good graces, and watch for his slip."

sentences.zh: 」烏孤乃受之。

translations.literal: Wugu then accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Wugu accepted.

sentences.zh: 烏孤討乙弗、折掘二部，大破之，遣其將石亦幹築廉川堡以都之。

translations.literal: Wugu campaigned against the Yifu and Zhejue tribes, routed them utterly, and sent his general Shiyi Gan to build Lianchuan Fort as his capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wugu attacked the Yifu and Zhejue tribes and broke them, then sent his general Shiyi Gan to build Lianchuan Fort and make it his seat.

sentences.zh: 烏孤登廉川大山，泣而不言。

translations.literal: Wugu ascended the great mountain at Lianchuan, weeping and saying nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Wugu climbed the great hill at Lianchuan and wept in silence.

sentences.zh: 石亦幹進曰：「臣聞主憂臣辱，主辱臣死，大王所為不樂者，將非呂光乎！

translations.literal: Shiyi Gan advanced and said, "I have heard that when the lord is troubled the minister is shamed, and when the lord is shamed the minister must die. What displeases you, great king—is it not Lü Guang?"
translations.idiomatic: Shiyi Gan stepped forward and said, "When the ruler grieves, the servant is disgraced; when the ruler is disgraced, the servant should die. Your grief, great king—is it not Lü Guang?"

sentences.zh: 光年已衰老，師徒屢敗。

translations.literal: Guang is already old, and his armies have suffered repeated defeats.
translations.idiomatic: Guang is aging, and his armies have been beaten again and again.

sentences.zh: 今我以士馬之盛，保據大川，乃可以一擊百，光何足懼也。

translations.literal: Now with the strength of our men and horses, holding the great rivers, we can strike one against a hundred—what is there to fear from Guang?"
translations.idiomatic: "With our strength in men and horses, holding the great rivers, we can meet a hundred with one—what is Guang to fear?"

sentences.zh: 」烏孤曰：「光之衰老，亦吾所知。

translations.literal: Wugu said, "Guang's aging—I know that too."
translations.idiomatic: Wugu said, "I know Guang is old."

sentences.zh: 但我祖宗以德懷遠，殊俗憚威，盧陵、契汗萬里委順。

translations.literal: But my forebears won distant peoples by virtue; foreign tribes feared their might, and Luling and Qihan submitted from a thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: "Yet my ancestors won distant peoples through virtue; barbarian tribes stood in awe of them, and Luling and Qihan submitted from a thousand li away."

sentences.zh: 及吾承業，諸部背叛，邇既乖違，遠何以附，所以泣耳。

translations.literal: When I inherited the enterprise, the tribes turned traitor; with those near in revolt, how can those far attach themselves? That is why I weep."
translations.idiomatic: "Since I took over, the tribes have rebelled. With the near in defiance, how can the far be won? That is why I weep."

sentences.zh: 」其將苻渾曰：「大王何不振旅誓眾，以討其罪。

translations.literal: His general Fu Hun said, "Great king, why not rouse the army and swear the host to punish their crime?"
translations.idiomatic: His general Fu Hun said, "Great king, why not raise the host and swear the army to punish their treason?"

sentences.zh: 」烏孤從之，大破諸部。

translations.literal: Wugu followed this and broke the tribes in great victory.
translations.idiomatic: Wugu took his advice and routed the rebel tribes.

sentences.zh: 呂光封烏孤廣武郡公。

translations.literal: Lü Guang enfeoffed Wugu as Duke of Guangwu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang made Wugu Duke of Guangwu commandery.

sentences.zh: 又討意雲鮮卑，大破之。

translations.literal: He also campaigned against the Yiyun Xianbei and defeated them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: He also attacked the Yiyun Xianbei and crushed them.

sentences.zh: 光又遣使署烏孤征南大將軍、益州牧、左賢王。

translations.literal: Guang again sent envoys to appoint Wugu Grand General Who Conquers the South, Governor of Yizhou, and Left Worthy King.
translations.idiomatic: Guang sent envoys again to name Wugu Grand General Who Conquers the South, governor of Yizhou, and Left Worthy King.

sentences.zh: 烏孤謂使者曰：「呂王昔以專征之威，遂有此州，不能以德柔遠，惠安黎庶。

translations.literal: Wugu told the envoys, "King Lü once used the authority of a special campaign to gain this province, yet he could not soften the distant by virtue or bring peace and kindness to the common people."
translations.idiomatic: Wugu told the envoys, "King Lü won this province by the sword alone, yet he never won the distant by kindness or eased the lot of the people."

sentences.zh: 諸子貪淫，三甥肆暴，郡縣土崩，下無生賴。

translations.literal: His sons are greedy and licentious; his three nephews by marriage are wantonly violent; commanderies and counties collapse, and below there is no livelihood for the people.
translations.idiomatic: His sons are greedy and dissolute; his three nephews by marriage run wild; the districts are crumbling and the people have nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 吾安可違天下之心，受不義之爵！

translations.literal: How can I go against the heart of the world and accept an unrighteous rank!"
translations.idiomatic: How can I defy the will of the realm and take a title built on injustice!"

sentences.zh: 帝王之起，豈有常哉！

translations.literal: The rise of emperors and kings—has that ever been fixed?"
translations.idiomatic: The rise of emperors and kings—is there ever a fixed rule?"

sentences.zh: 無道則滅，有德則昌，吾將順天人之望，為天下主。

translations.literal: Without the Way they perish; with virtue they flourish. I shall follow the hope of Heaven and men and become lord of the world."
translations.idiomatic: The lawless fall and the virtuous prevail. I will follow Heaven and the people and become master of the realm."

sentences.zh: 」留其鼓吹羽儀，謝其使而遣之。

translations.literal: He kept their drums, pipes, banners, and regalia, thanked the envoys, and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: He kept their drums, pipes, banners, and regalia, thanked the envoys, and dismissed them.

sentences.zh: 烏孤從容謂其群下曰：「隴右區區數郡地耳！

translations.literal: Wugu said calmly to his followers, "Longyou is only a few commanderies!"
translations.idiomatic: Wugu said calmly to his followers, "Longyou is only a handful of commanderies!"

sentences.zh: 因其兵亂，分裂遂至十餘。

translations.literal: Because of their military disorder they split until there were more than ten.
translations.idiomatic: Their wars have splintered them into more than a dozen states.

sentences.zh: 乾歸擅命河南，段業阻兵張掖，虐氐假息，偷據姑臧。

translations.literal: Qifu Gangui acts on his own south of the Yellow River; Duan Ye blocks the roads at Zhangye with arms; the cruel Di usurper Lü Guang clings to Guzang by stealth.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Gangui rules Henan on his own authority; Duan Ye holds Zhangye by force; the cruel Di pretender Lü Guang has stolen Guzang.

sentences.zh: 吾藉父兄遣烈。

translations.literal: I rely on the heroic legacy my father and elder brothers left behind.
translations.idiomatic: I have my father and brothers' heroic deeds to build on.

sentences.zh: 思郭清西夏。

translations.literal: I intend to pacify the western domains.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to bring order to the western lands.

sentences.zh: 兼弱攻昧，三者何先？

translations.literal: To attack the weak and strike the benighted—which of the three should come first?"
translations.idiomatic: To overwhelm the weak and strike down the blind—which of these three should we take first?"

sentences.zh: 」楊統進曰：「乾歸本我所部，終必歸服。

translations.literal: Yang Tong advanced and said, "Gangui was originally of our following and will in the end submit."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tong stepped forward and said, "Gangui was once our vassal and will submit in the end."

sentences.zh: 段業儒生，才非經世，權臣擅命，制不由已，千里伐人，糧運懸絕，且與我鄰好，許以分災共患，乘其危弊，非義舉也。

translations.literal: Duan Ye is a Confucian scholar, his talent not fit to order the age; powerful ministers act on their own and he cannot command them. To campaign a thousand li, grain transport cut off, and moreover he is our neighbor in friendship, having promised to share disaster and peril—to strike him in his distress is not a righteous act."
translations.idiomatic: "Duan Ye is a bookish man, unfit to govern an age; his strongmen do as they please and he cannot control them. A thousand-li campaign with supply lines severed—and he is our neighbor, pledged to share hardship—would be an unrighteous blow at a weakened friend."

sentences.zh: 呂光衰老，嗣紹沖暗，二子纂、弘，雖頗有文武，而內相猜忌。

translations.literal: Lü Guang is old; his heir Shao is young and dull; his two sons Zuan and Hong, though both have some civil and military ability, are mutually suspicious within."
translations.idiomatic: "Lü Guang is old; his heir Shao is young and dim; his sons Zuan and Hong have talent in arms and statecraft, yet they mistrust one another."

sentences.zh: 若天威臨之，必應鋒瓦解。

translations.literal: If Heaven's majesty presses upon them, they will surely crumble at the first clash.
translations.idiomatic: "If our power falls on them, they will break at a touch."

sentences.zh: 宜遣車騎鎮浩亹，鎮北據廉川，乘虛迭出，多方以誤之，救右則擊其左，救左則擊其右，使纂疲於奔命，人不得安其農業。

translations.literal: You should send the chariot-and-cavalry commander to hold Haoqian, and the north-pacifying commander to hold Lianchuan; strike from emptiness in succession, confuse them on many fronts—if they rescue the right, strike the left; if they rescue the left, strike the right—so that Zuan wears himself out running to and fro and the people cannot tend their fields.
translations.idiomatic: "Post the chariot-and-cavalry commander at Haoqian and the north-pacifying commander on the Lianchuan line; raid in turn wherever they are thin, feint on many fronts—relieve their right and hit their left, relieve their left and hit their right—until Zuan is worn out running about and the people cannot farm in peace."

sentences.zh: 兼弱攻昧，於是乎在，不出二年，可以坐定姑臧。

translations.literal: To attack the weak and strike the benighted lies in this; within two years Guzang can be settled without stirring from your seat.
translations.idiomatic: "Attack the weak and strike the blind—that is the way. Within two years Guzang can be taken without your leaving the seat."

sentences.zh: 姑臧既拔，二寇不待兵戈，自然服矣。

translations.literal: Once Guzang is taken, the other two foes will submit without waiting for arms.
translations.idiomatic: "Once Guzang falls, the other two enemies will yield without a fight."

sentences.zh: 」烏孤然之，遂陰有吞併之志。

translations.literal: Wugu agreed and secretly cherished the ambition to swallow them up.
translations.idiomatic: Wugu agreed and secretly resolved on conquest.

sentences.zh: 段業為呂纂所侵，遣利鹿孤救之。

translations.literal: Duan Ye was harried by Lü Zuan and sent Lilugu to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ye, pressed by Lü Zuan, asked Lilugu for relief.

sentences.zh: 纂懼，燒氐池、張掖穀麥而還。

translations.literal: Zuan, afraid, burned the grain in Dichí and Zhangye and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan, alarmed, burned the grain stores of Dichí and Zhangye and retreated.

sentences.zh: 以利鹿孤為涼州牧，鎮西平，追傉檀入錄府國事。

translations.literal: He appointed Lilugu Governor of Liangzhou to hold Xiping and recalled Rutan to manage state affairs at court.
translations.idiomatic: He made Lilugu governor of Liangzhou at Xiping and called Rutan back to handle affairs at court.

sentences.zh: 是歲，烏孤因酒墜馬傷脅，笑曰：「幾使呂光父子大喜。

translations.literal: That year Wugu, drunk, fell from his horse and injured his side; he laughed and said, "I nearly gave Lü Guang and his sons great joy."
translations.idiomatic: That year Wugu, drunk, fell from his horse and hurt his ribs. He laughed and said, "I nearly made Lü Guang and his sons very happy."

sentences.zh: 」俄而患甚，顧謂群下曰：「方難未靜，宜立長君。

translations.literal: Soon his illness grew grave; he looked at his followers and said, "The troubles are not yet settled—a mature ruler should be set up."
translations.idiomatic: Soon he worsened. He told his followers, "The realm is still unsettled; you must raise a seasoned ruler."

sentences.zh: 」言終而死，在王位三年，偽諡武王，廟號烈祖。

translations.literal: When he had spoken he died. He had reigned three years; his posthumous title was King Wu and his temple name Liezu.
translations.idiomatic: He died as he finished speaking. He had ruled three years; his posthumous title was King Wu and his temple name Founder Lie.

sentences.zh: 弟利鹿孤立。

translations.literal: His younger brother Lilugu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Lilugu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 禿髮利鹿孤

translations.literal: Tufa Lilugu
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Lilugu

sentences.zh: 利鹿孤以隆安三年即偽位，赦其境內殊死已下，又徙居於西平。

translations.literal: Lilugu took the false throne in the third year of Long'an, pardoned all within his borders below capital offense, and moved his seat to Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Long'an Lilugu took the throne, pardoned all crimes short of capital offense within his realm, and moved his capital to Xiping.

sentences.zh: 使記室監麹梁明聘于段業。

translations.literal: He sent Registrar Qu Liangming on a mission to Duan Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his registrar Qu Liangming as envoy to Duan Ye.

sentences.zh: 業曰：「貴主先王創業啟運，功高先世，宜為國之太祖，有子何以不立？

translations.literal: Ye said, "Your former king founded the enterprise and opened the mandate; his merit towers above earlier ages. He ought to be the dynastic founder. You have a son—why do you not enthrone him?"
translations.idiomatic: Ye said, "Your late king opened the enterprise; his merit outshines the past. He should be dynastic founder. You have a son—why not set him on the throne?"

sentences.zh: 」梁明曰：「有子羌奴，先王之命也。

translations.literal: Liangming said, "There is a son, Qiangnu—it was the late king's command."
translations.idiomatic: Liangming said, "There is a son, Qiangnu, as the late king commanded."

sentences.zh: 」業曰：「昔成王弱齡，周召作宰；

translations.literal: Ye said, "In former times King Cheng was young and the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao served as regents;"
translations.idiomatic: Ye said, "King Cheng of Zhou was young, yet the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao ruled as regents;"

sentences.zh: 漢昭八歲，金、霍夾輔。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhao of Han was eight, and Jin Ri and Huo Guang assisted him on either side.
translations.idiomatic: Han Emperor Zhao was eight, and Jin Ri and Huo Guang flanked him in support.

sentences.zh: 雖嗣子沖幼，而二叔休明，左提右挈，不亦可乎？

translations.literal: Though the heir is young, the two uncles are enlightened—why not guide him left and right? Is that not possible?"
translations.idiomatic: "Though the heir is young, two able uncles could guide him—would that not serve?"

sentences.zh: 」明曰：「宋宣能以國讓，《春秋》美之；

translations.literal: Ming said, "Duke Xuan of Song yielded the state, and the Spring and Autumn Annals praise him;"
translations.idiomatic: Ming said, "Duke Xuan of Song gave up the state, and the Spring and Autumn Annals honor him;"

sentences.zh: 孫伯符委事仲謀，終開有吳之業。

translations.literal: Sun Ce entrusted affairs to Sun Quan, and in the end he opened the Wu enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce handed power to Sun Quan and in the end founded Wu.

sentences.zh: 且兄終弟及，殷湯之制也，亦聖人之格言，萬代之通式，何必胤已為是，紹兄為非。

translations.literal: Moreover, elder brother dying and younger succeeding is the institution of Tang of Yin—it is also the sage's maxim and the universal pattern for ten thousand generations. Why must passing to a son be right and following an elder brother be wrong?"
translations.idiomatic: "Elder yielding to younger was Tang of Yin's rule—a sage's maxim and the pattern of ages. Why must a son succeed and an elder brother be wrong?"

sentences.zh: 」業曰：「美哉！

translations.literal: Ye said, "Beautiful!"
translations.idiomatic: Ye said, "Well spoken!"

sentences.zh: 使乎之義也。」

translations.literal: The meaning of an envoy indeed."
translations.idiomatic: That is the duty of an envoy."

sentences.zh: 利鹿孤聞呂光死，遣其將金樹、蘇翹率騎五千屯於昌松漠口。

translations.literal: When Lilugu heard that Lü Guang had died, he sent his generals Jin Shu and Su Qiao with five thousand horsemen to encamp at the mouth of the Changsong desert.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Lü Guang's death, Lilugu sent his generals Jin Shu and Su Qiao with five thousand horse to camp at the mouth of the Changsong desert.

sentences.zh: 既逾年，赦其境內，改元曰建和。

translations.literal: After a year had passed he pardoned all within his borders and changed the era name to Jianhe.
translations.idiomatic: After another year he proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Jianhe.

sentences.zh: 二千石長吏清高有惠化者，皆封亭侯、關內侯。

translations.literal: All prefectural and county officials of two thousand piculs and above who were upright and had brought kindly rule were enfeoffed as marquises of a ting or as marquises within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Every prefect or magistrate of two thousand piculs and above who had governed uprightly with kindness was enfeoffed as a ting marquis or a marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 呂纂來伐，使傉檀距之。

translations.literal: Lü Zuan came to attack; Lilugu sent Rutan to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan marched against him; Lilugu sent Rutan to meet him.

sentences.zh: 纂士卒精銳，進度三堆，三軍擾懼。

translations.literal: Zuan's troops were elite; as he advanced past the Three Mounds the whole army was alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's soldiers were crack troops; crossing the Three Mounds they threw the army into fear.

sentences.zh: 傉檀下馬據胡床而坐，士眾心乃始安。

translations.literal: Rutan dismounted and sat on a folding chair; only then did the host's hearts grow steady.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan dismounted and sat on a camp stool, and the troops steadied.

sentences.zh: 與纂戰，敗之，斬二千餘級。

translations.literal: He fought Zuan, defeated him, and beheaded more than two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He gave battle, routed Zuan, and took more than two thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 纂西擊段業，傉檀率騎一萬，乘虛襲姑臧。

translations.literal: Zuan struck west at Duan Ye; Rutan led ten thousand horse and struck Guzang in his absence.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan marched west against Duan Ye; Rutan led ten thousand horse and raided Guzang while he was away.

sentences.zh: 纂弟緯守南北城以自固。

translations.literal: Zuan's younger brother Wei held the southern and northern cities to defend himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's brother Wei held the inner and outer cities of Guzang.

sentences.zh: 傉檀置酒於硃明門上，鳴鐘鼓以饗將士，耀兵于青陽門，虜八千餘戶而歸。

translations.literal: Rutan set out wine at the Vermilion Bright Gate, sounded bells and drums to feast his officers, displayed his army at the Green Yang Gate, and carried off more than eight thousand households on his return.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan feasted his officers with wine at the Vermilion Bright Gate, beat drums at the Green Yang Gate to display his strength, and withdrew with more than eight thousand households.

sentences.zh: 乞伏乾歸為姚興所敗，率騎數百來奔，處之晉興，待以上賓之禮。

translations.literal: Qifu Gangui was defeated by Yao Xing and came fleeing with several hundred horse; Lilugu settled him at Jinxing and treated him with the courtesy due a chief guest.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Gangui, beaten by Yao Xing, fled with a few hundred horse; Lilugu lodged him at Jinxing and honored him as a chief guest.

sentences.zh: 乾歸遣子謙等質于西平。

translations.literal: Gangui sent his son Qian and others as hostages to Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui sent his son Qian and others as hostages to Xiping.

sentences.zh: 鎮北將軍俱延言于利鹿孤曰：「乾歸本我之屬國，妄自尊立，理窮歸命，非有款誠；

translations.literal: The north-pacifying commander Ju Yan said to Lilugu, "Gangui was originally our dependent state; he set himself up without right, and when his case was exhausted he came in submission—not from sincere goodwill;"
translations.idiomatic: The north-pacifying commander Ju Yan told Lilugu, "Gangui was our vassal who proclaimed himself without warrant; driven to the wall he submits, not from true loyalty;"

sentences.zh: 若奔東秦，必引師西侵，非我利也。

translations.literal: if he flees to Eastern Qin he will surely lead their armies west—that is no gain for us."
translations.idiomatic: "if he escapes to Eastern Qin he will bring their armies west, which cannot profit us."

sentences.zh: 宜徙於乙弗之間，防其越逸之路。

translations.literal: He should be moved among the Yifu to block his route of escape."
translations.idiomatic: "Move him among the Yifu and cut off his path of flight."

sentences.zh: 」利鹿孤曰：「吾方弘信義以收天下之心，乾歸投誠而徙之，四海將謂我不可以誠信託也。

translations.literal: Lilugu said, "I am now broadening faith and righteousness to win the hearts of the world; if Gangui comes in trust and I move him, the four seas will say I cannot be trusted with good faith."
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu said, "I am winning the realm by faith; if Gangui submits in trust and I uproot him, all will say I cannot be trusted."

sentences.zh: 」俄而乾歸果奔于姚興。

translations.literal: Before long Gangui indeed fled to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Gangui did flee to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 利鹿孤謂延曰：「不用卿言，乾歸果叛，卿為吾行也。

translations.literal: Lilugu said to Yan, "Had I not taken your counsel, Gangui would indeed have rebelled. You must go after him for me."
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu told Yan, "Had I listened to you, Gangui would have betrayed us. Go after him for me."

sentences.zh: 」延追乾歸至河，不及而還。

translations.literal: Yan pursued Gangui to the river but could not overtake him and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yan chased Gangui to the river, failed to catch him, and returned.

sentences.zh: 利鹿孤立二年，龍見於長寧，麒麟游於綏羌，於是群臣勸進，以隆安五年僭稱河西王。

translations.literal: In Lilugu's second year a dragon appeared at Changning and a qilin roamed at Suiqiang; the ministers therefore urged him to advance, and in the fifth year of Long'an he presumptuously styled himself King of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: In Lilugu's second year a dragon was seen at Changning and a qilin at Suiqiang; his ministers urged elevation, and in the fifth year of Long'an he took the title King of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 其將鍮勿侖進曰：「昔我先君肇自幽、朔，被髮左衽，無冠冕之義，遷徙不常，無城邑之制，用能中分天下，威振殊境。

translations.literal: His general Chouwu Lun advanced and said, "In former times our first lord rose from You and Shu, with hair unbound and garments folded to the left, without the rites of cap and crown, migrating without fixed abode, without the system of walled cities—yet he could divide the realm in two and make his might felt across foreign lands."
translations.idiomatic: His general Chouwu Lun said, "Our first lords rose from You and Shu with hair unbound and garments to the left, knowing neither caps nor courts nor fixed cities—yet they split the realm and made their power felt beyond the border."

sentences.zh: 今建大號，誠順天心。

translations.literal: Now to establish a great title is truly to follow Heaven's heart.
translations.idiomatic: "To raise a great title now truly follows Heaven's will."

sentences.zh: 然甯居樂士，非貽厥之規；

translations.literal: Yet to dwell at ease on rich soil is not a plan to hand down to posterity;"
translations.idiomatic: "Yet ease on rich land is no legacy for sons and grandsons;"

sentences.zh: 倉府粟帛，生敵人之志。

translations.literal: grain in the storehouses and silk in the treasury only stir the enemy's ambition."
translations.idiomatic: "full granaries and treasuries only whet the enemy's appetite."

sentences.zh: 且首兵始號，事必無成，陳勝、項籍，前鑒不遠。

translations.literal: Moreover, he who first raises arms and first proclaims a title will surely not succeed; Chen Sheng and Xiang Yu are warnings not far off."
translations.idiomatic: "He who first takes up arms and first proclaims a title seldom succeeds—Chen Sheng and Xiang Yu are warnings near at hand."

sentences.zh: 宜置晉人于諸城，勸課農桑，以供軍國之用，我則習戰法以誅未賓。

translations.literal: The Jin people should be placed in the various cities to urge farming and sericulture for the supply of the army and state; we should drill in warfare to punish those not yet submitted."
translations.idiomatic: "Settle the Jin people in the towns to farm and feed army and state; we ourselves should train for war and subdue those not yet bowed."

sentences.zh: 若東西有變，長算以縻之；

translations.literal: If trouble arises east or west, long-range plans can tie them down;
translations.idiomatic: If trouble flares east or west, distant strategy can hold them in check;

sentences.zh: 如其敵強於我，徙而以避其鋒，不亦善乎！

translations.literal: if the enemy is stronger than we, move away to avoid their edge—is that not also good!"
translations.idiomatic: and if they outmatch us, shift ground and avoid their edge—would that not serve as well!"

sentences.zh: 」利鹿孤然其言。

translations.literal: Lilugu approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu agreed with him.

sentences.zh: 於是率師伐呂隆，大敗之，獲其右僕射楊桓。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led the army to campaign against Lü Long, routed him utterly, and captured his Right Vice Director Yang Huan.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched against Lü Long, broke him, and took his right vice director Yang Huan.

sentences.zh: 傉檀謂之曰：「安寢危邦，不思擇木，老為囚虜，豈曰智也！

translations.literal: Rutan said to him, "You sleep at ease in a perilous state and never thought to choose a new perch; in old age you are a captive—is that wisdom?"
translations.idiomatic: Rutan told him, "You rested easy in a doomed realm and never chose a safer master; now, old and a prisoner, can you call that wisdom?"

sentences.zh: 」桓曰：「受呂氏厚恩，位忝端貳，雖洪水滔天，猶欲濟彼俱溺，實恥為叛臣以見明主。

translations.literal: Huan said, "I received great favor from the Lü clan and held the second rank; though floods rise to heaven I would still try to save them together—I would be ashamed to appear before a wise lord as a rebel minister."
translations.idiomatic: Huan said, "The Lü treated me generously and I held the second rank; even if floods covered heaven I would still try to drown with them—I could not face a worthy ruler as a turncoat."

sentences.zh: 」傉檀曰：「卿忠臣也！

translations.literal: Rutan said, "You are a loyal minister!"
translations.idiomatic: Rutan said, "You are a loyal man!"

sentences.zh: 」以為左司馬。

translations.literal: He made him Left Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed him Left Marshal.

sentences.zh: 利鹿孤謂其群下曰：「吾無經濟之才，忝承業統，自負乘在位，三載於茲。

translations.literal: Lilugu said to his followers, "I have no talent for ordering the state yet shamefully inherit the enterprise; since I took the throne three years have passed."
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu told his ministers, "I lack the talent to govern yet hold the throne; three years have passed since I succeeded."

sentences.zh: 雖夙夜惟寅，思弘道化，而刑政未能允中，風俗尚多凋弊；

translations.literal: Though day and night I am reverent, thinking to spread the Way and transform, punishments and government are not yet fair, and customs still decay greatly;"
translations.idiomatic: "Though I labor day and night to spread the Way, justice is not yet even and customs still decay;"

sentences.zh: 戎車屢駕，無辟境之功；

translations.literal: war chariots are driven again and again, yet there is no achievement in opening borders;"
translations.idiomatic: "armies march again and again, yet we win no new ground;"

sentences.zh: 務進賢彥，而下猶蓄滯。

translations.literal: I strive to advance worthy men, yet below there is still stagnation.
translations.idiomatic: "I seek worthy men, yet talent still languishes below."

sentences.zh: 豈所任非才，將吾不明所致也？

translations.literal: Is it that those I employ lack ability, or that my own lack of clarity causes this?"
translations.idiomatic: "Have I chosen the wrong men, or is my own blindness to blame?"

sentences.zh: 二三君子其極言無諱，吾將覽焉。

translations.literal: You gentlemen, speak without reserve—I shall read your words."
translations.idiomatic: "Speak plainly, all of you—I will hear it."

sentences.zh: 」祠部郎中史暠對曰：「古之王者，行師以全軍為上，破國次之，拯溺救焚，東征西怨。

translations.literal: Palace Officer Shi Hao replied, "Ancient kings, when they marched, prized preserving the whole army highest, taking a state second, rescuing the drowning and saving the burning; east or west the people complained."
translations.idiomatic: Palace officer Shi Hao answered, "Ancient kings, when they took the field, prized sparing the army above all, conquering states second, rescuing the drowning and quenching fire; whether they marched east or west, the people had grievances."

sentences.zh: 今不以綏寧為先，惟以徙戶為務，安土重遷，故有離叛，所以斬將克城，土不加廣。

translations.literal: Now you do not put peace first but make moving households your task; the people love their soil and dread removal, hence there is defection—thus though you behead generals and take cities, the land does not grow."
translations.idiomatic: "Today you do not put peace first but uproot the people; they love their homes and resist removal, so they rebel—thus you may take cities yet your domain does not widen."

sentences.zh: 今取士拔才，必先弓馬，文章學藝為無用之條，非所以來遠人，垂不朽也。

translations.literal: In choosing scholars and raising talent you first demand bow and horse; letters and arts count as useless—this is not how to draw distant men or leave a lasting name."
translations.idiomatic: "You choose men by bow and horse alone and treat learning as useless—that will not draw the distant or win lasting fame."

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：'不學禮，無以立。

translations.literal: Confucius said, 'Without learning ritual, one cannot stand.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, 'Without ritual, a man cannot stand.'

sentences.zh: '宜建學校，開庠序，選耆德碩儒以訓胄子。

translations.literal: 'You should build schools, open academies, and choose venerable great scholars to instruct the crown prince's sons.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Build schools, open halls of learning, and set venerable scholars to teach the sons of the realm.'

sentences.zh: 」利鹿孤善之，於是以田玄沖、趙誕為博士祭酒，以教胄子。

translations.literal: Lilugu approved this and thereupon made Tian Xuanchong and Zhao Yan libationers and masters to teach the crown princes.
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu agreed and appointed Tian Xuanchong and Zhao Yan libationers to instruct the royal youths.

sentences.zh: 時利鹿孤雖僭位，尚臣姚興。

translations.literal: At that time, though Lilugu had usurped the title, he still served Yao Xing as a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Though Lilugu had taken a royal title, he still acknowledged Yao Xing as suzerain.

sentences.zh: 楊桓兄經佐命姚萇，早死，興聞桓有德望，征之。

translations.literal: Yang Huan's elder brother Jing had aided Yao Chang and died early; Xing heard that Huan had virtue and summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huan's elder brother Jing had served Yao Chang and died young; when Xing heard of Huan's reputation he summoned him.

sentences.zh: 利鹿孤餞桓於城東，謂之曰：「本期與卿共成大業，事乖本圖，分歧之感，實情深古人。

translations.literal: Lilugu saw Huan off east of the city and said to him, "I had hoped to achieve the great enterprise with you; affairs have gone against the original plan—the pain of parting is truly as deep as the ancients felt."
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu feasted Huan east of the city and said, "I meant to build the great enterprise with you; fate has turned—this parting cuts as deep as any in the histories."

sentences.zh: 但鯤非溟海，無以運其軀；

translations.literal: But the kun is not the dark sea and cannot move its body;
translations.idiomatic: "The great fish is not the ocean deep and cannot swim there;

sentences.zh: 鳳非修梧，無以晞其翼。

translations.literal: the phoenix is not the tall paulownia and cannot dry its wings.
translations.idiomatic: the phoenix is not the sacred tree and cannot spread its wings."

sentences.zh: 卿有佐時之器，夜光之寶，當振纓雲閣，耀價連城，區區河右，未足以逞卿才力。

translations.literal: You have the talent to aid the age and the treasure of night-shining jade; you should shake your tassels at the Cloud Pavilion and shine in price like linked cities—the mere Hexi right bank is not enough to display your power.
translations.idiomatic: "You have talent for the times and jewels that shine in the dark; you belong in the halls of empire, worth cities in ransom—Hexi alone cannot hold you."

sentences.zh: 善勖日新，以成大美。

translations.literal: Strive daily toward renewal to complete the great beauty."
translations.idiomatic: "Press on daily and fulfill your promise."

sentences.zh: 」桓泣曰：「臣往事呂氏，情節不建。

translations.literal: Huan wept and said, "I formerly served the Lü clan and achieved no merit."
translations.idiomatic: Huan wept and said, "I served the Lü and achieved nothing for them."

sentences.zh: 陛下宥臣于俘虜之中，顯同賢舊，每希攀龍附風，立尺寸之功，龍門既開，而臣違離，公衡之戀，豈曰忘之！

translations.literal: Your Majesty spared me among the captives and honored me like an old worthy; I always hoped to climb the dragon and cling to the wind and establish merit however small. The dragon gate is now open yet I must leave—the longing of Gongheng—how could I forget it!"
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty raised me from captivity and treated me as an old friend; I hoped to rise with you and do some small service. The gate is open yet I must go—the tie to a true lord—how could I forget it!"

sentences.zh: 」利鹿孤為之流涕。

translations.literal: Lilugu wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu wept with him.

sentences.zh: 遣傉檀又攻呂隆昌松太守孟禕于顯美，克之。

translations.literal: He sent Rutan again to attack Lü Long's Changsong prefect Meng Yi at Xianmei and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Rutan to attack Lü Long's Changsong prefect Meng Yi at Xianmei and took the place.

sentences.zh: 傉檀執禕而數之曰：「見機而作，賞之所先；

translations.literal: Rutan seized Yi and rebuked him, saying, "To act when you see the moment is what reward honors first;"
translations.idiomatic: Rutan seized Yi and said, "To seize the moment wins reward;"

sentences.zh: 守迷不變，刑之所及。

translations.literal: to hold to error and not change is what punishment reaches.
translations.idiomatic: "to cling to error invites punishment."

sentences.zh: 吾方耀威玉門，掃平秦、隴，卿固守窮城，稽淹王憲，國有常刑，于分甘乎？

translations.literal: I am about to display might at the Jade Gate and sweep Qin and Long; you stubbornly hold a desperate city and delay the royal command—does the state's constant punishment suit your station?"
translations.idiomatic: "I will show my might at the Jade Gate and sweep Qin and Long; you held a doomed town against the royal command—do you accept the law's due?"

sentences.zh: 」禕曰：「明公開翦河右，聲播宇內，文德以綏遠人，威武以懲不恪，況禕蔑爾，敢距天命！

translations.literal: Yi said, "The enlightened lord has cut down Hexi and his fame fills the realm; with civil virtue he soothes the distant and with martial might he punishes the unyielding—how could Yi, so slight, dare resist Heaven's mandate!"
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "Your lordship has conquered Hexi and your name fills the realm; civil virtue wins the distant and martial might punishes the proud—how could I, a nobody, resist Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 釁鼓之刑，禕之分也。

translations.literal: The punishment of the war drum is Yi's portion.
translations.idiomatic: "The drum of war is my due."

sentences.zh: 但忠於彼者，亦忠於此。

translations.literal: But he who is loyal there is also loyal here.
translations.idiomatic: "Loyalty to one master is loyalty to another."

sentences.zh: 荷呂氏厚恩，受籓屏之任，明公至而歸命，恐獲罪于執事，惟公圖之。

translations.literal: I received great favor from the Lü clan and bore the duty of a frontier shield; when the enlightened lord came I submitted, fearing guilt before your staff—only your lordship may judge."
translations.idiomatic: "The Lü favored me with a frontier post; when you came I submitted, fearing I might seem a traitor—only you can judge."

sentences.zh: 」傉檀大悅，釋其縛，待之客禮。

translations.literal: Rutan was greatly pleased, released his bonds, and treated him with guest courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan was delighted, freed him, and honored him as a guest.

sentences.zh: 徙顯美、麗靬二千餘戶而歸。

translations.literal: He moved more than two thousand households from Xianmei and Ligan and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He resettled more than two thousand households from Xianmei and Ligan and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 嘉禕忠烈，拜左司馬。

translations.literal: Honoring Yi's loyal integrity, he appointed him Left Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Praising Yi's loyalty, he made him Left Marshal.

sentences.zh: 禕請曰：「呂氏將亡，聖朝之並河右，昭然已定。

translations.literal: Yi requested, saying, "The Lü clan is about to perish; the holy court's possession of Hexi is already clear."
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "The Lü are finished; your taking of Hexi is already plain."

sentences.zh: 但為人守而不全，復忝顯任，竊所未安。

translations.literal: Yet to guard for others and not succeed, then to bear a lofty post again—I have never been at ease with it.
translations.idiomatic: "I held a post I could not keep; to take honor again shames me."

sentences.zh: 明公之恩，聽禕就戮于姑臧，死且不朽。

translations.literal: By the enlightened lord's grace, grant that Yi may meet execution at Guzang—death would be undying."
translations.idiomatic: "By your grace let me die at Guzang—that death would be immortal."

sentences.zh: 」傉檀義而許之。

translations.literal: Rutan, moved by righteousness, granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan, respecting his honor, agreed.

sentences.zh: 呂隆為沮渠蒙遜所伐，遣使乞師，利鹿孤引群下議之。

translations.literal: Lü Long was attacked by Juqu Mengxun and sent envoys begging for troops; Lilugu gathered his ministers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun attacked Lü Long, who begged for aid; Lilugu called his ministers to counsel.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞婆衍侖曰：「今姑臧饑荒殘弊，谷石萬錢，野無青草，資食無取。

translations.literal: Left Director of the Masters of Writing Poyan Lun said, "Now Guzang is famine-stricken and ruined; grain is ten thousand cash a picul and there is no green grass in the wilds—supplies cannot be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Director Poyan Lun said, "Guzang is starving; grain costs ten thousand cash a picul and the fields are bare—there is nothing to feed an army."

sentences.zh: 蒙遜千里行師，糧運不屬，使二寇相殘，以乘其釁。

translations.literal: Mengxun marches a thousand li; grain transport cannot follow—let the two foes wear each other down and strike at their lapse."
translations.idiomatic: "Mengxun marches a thousand li without supplies—let the two enemies weaken each other and strike when they falter."

sentences.zh: 若蒙遜拔姑臧，亦不能守，適可為吾取之，不宜救也。

translations.literal: If Mengxun takes Guzang he also cannot hold it—it will simply be taken for us; we should not rescue."
translations.idiomatic: "If Mengxun takes Guzang he cannot hold it—we should take it ourselves, not rescue Long."

sentences.zh: 」傉檀曰：「侖知其一，未知其二。

translations.literal: Rutan said, "Lun knows one thing but not the second."
translations.idiomatic: Rutan said, "Lun sees one side only."

sentences.zh: 姑臧今雖虛弊，地居形勝，可西一都之會，不可使蒙遜據之，宜在速救。

translations.literal: Though Guzang is now weak and ruined, its ground holds strategic advantage—it is the western meeting place of capitals and cannot be left to Mengxun; we should rescue quickly."
translations.idiomatic: "Guzang is weak but its ground is strong—the western hub of realms. Mengxun must not hold it; we must rescue at once."

sentences.zh: 」利鹿孤曰：「車騎之言，吾之心也。

translations.literal: Lilugu said, "The chariot-and-cavalry commander's words are my own heart."
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu said, "The chariot commander's words are my own mind."

sentences.zh: 」遂遣傉檀率騎一萬救之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Rutan with ten thousand horse to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Rutan with ten thousand horse to relieve Long.

sentences.zh: 至昌松而蒙遜已退，傉檀徙涼澤、段塚五百餘家而歸。

translations.literal: When he reached Changsong, Mengxun had already withdrawn; Rutan moved more than five hundred households from Liangze and Duandui and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At Changsong Mengxun had already withdrawn; Rutan resettled five hundred households from Liangze and Duandui and returned.

sentences.zh: 利鹿孤寢疾，令曰：「內外多虞，國機務廣，其令車騎嗣業，以成先王之志。

translations.literal: Lilugu fell ill and ordered, "Within and without there are many troubles and state affairs are weighty—let the chariot-and-cavalry commander succeed to the enterprise to fulfill the former king's will."
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu fell ill and commanded, "Trouble presses within and without; let the chariot commander succeed and fulfill our father's will."

sentences.zh: 」在位三年而死，葬于西平之東南，偽諡曰康王。

translations.literal: He had reigned three years and died; he was buried southeast of Xiping; his posthumous title was King Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He had ruled three years and died; he was buried southeast of Xiping with the posthumous name King Kang.

sentences.zh: 弟傉檀嗣。

translations.literal: His younger brother Rutan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Rutan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 禿髮傉檀

translations.literal: Tufa Rutan
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Tufa Rutan

sentences.zh: 傉檀少機警，有才略。

translations.literal: Rutan in youth was quick-witted and had talent and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan was quick and resourceful from youth.

sentences.zh: 其父奇之，謂諸子曰：「傉檀明識幹藝，非汝等輩也。

translations.literal: His father marveled at him and told his sons, "Rutan's clear insight and practical skill are not your class."
translations.idiomatic: His father said to his sons, "Rutan's vision and ability are not yours."

sentences.zh: 」是以諸兄不以授子，欲傳之于傉檀。

translations.literal: Therefore the elder brothers did not pass the realm to their sons but wished to transmit it to Rutan.
translations.idiomatic: So the elder brothers meant the realm for Rutan, not their own sons.

sentences.zh: 及利鹿孤即位，垂拱而已，軍國大事皆以委之。

translations.literal: When Lilugu took the throne he merely held court; all great affairs of army and state were entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lilugu reigned he held court in name only; Rutan ran army and state.

sentences.zh: 以元興元年僭號涼王，遷于樂都，改元曰弘昌。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanxing he presumptuously styled himself King of Liang, moved to Ledu, and changed the era name to Hongchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanxing he took the title King of Liang, moved the capital to Ledu, and proclaimed the era Hongchang.

sentences.zh: 初，乞伏乾歸之在晉興也，以世子熾磐為質。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Qifu Gangui was at Jinxing, he had left his heir Chibpan as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: When Qifu Gangui had been at Jinxing, he left his heir Chibpan as hostage.

sentences.zh: 後熾磐逃歸，為追騎所執，利鹿孤命殺之。

translations.literal: Later Chibpan fled back and was seized by pursuing horsemen; Lilugu ordered him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Chibpan later fled home and was caught by pursuers; Lilugu ordered his death.

sentences.zh: 傉檀曰：「臣子逃歸君父，振古通義，故魏武善關羽之奔，秦昭恕頃襄之逝。

translations.literal: Rutan said, "For a minister or son to flee back to lord and father is a universal principle of old; thus Cao Wu favored Guan Yu's flight and Qin Zhao forgave King Xiang of Chu's departure."
translations.idiomatic: Rutan said, "A son who flees to his father follows the oldest law; Cao Cao honored Guan Yu's return and King Zhao of Qin spared King Xiang of Chu."

sentences.zh: 熾磐雖逃叛，孝心可嘉，宜垂全宥，以弘海嶽之量。

translations.literal: Though Chibpan fled in rebellion, his filial heart is praiseworthy; he should receive full pardon to extend the measure of sea and mountain."
translations.idiomatic: "Chibpan fled from loyalty to kinship—that deserves mercy, not death."

sentences.zh: 」乃赦之。

translations.literal: He was then pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 至是，熾磐又奔允街，傉檀歸其妻子。

translations.literal: By this time Chibpan had fled again to Yunjie; Rutan returned his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: When Chibpan fled again to Yunjie, Rutan sent back his family.

sentences.zh: 姚興遣使拜傉檀車騎將軍、廣武公。

translations.literal: Yao Xing sent envoys to appoint Rutan General of Chariots and Cavalry and Duke of Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing sent envoys naming Rutan General of Chariots and Cavalry and Duke of Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 傉檀大城樂都。

translations.literal: Rutan greatly fortified Ledu.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan greatly expanded the walls of Ledu.

sentences.zh: 姚興遣將齊難率眾迎呂隆于姑臧，傉檀攝昌松、魏安二戍以避之。

translations.literal: Yao Xing sent General Qi Nan with troops to welcome Lü Long at Guzang; Rutan took over the garrisons of Changsong and Wei'an to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: Xing sent General Qi Nan to install Lü Long at Guzang; Rutan seized the garrisons of Changsong and Wei'an to give way.

sentences.zh: 興涼州刺史王尚遣主薄宗敞來聘。

translations.literal: Xing's Liangzhou inspector Wang Shang sent Registrar Zong Chang on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shang, Xing's inspector of Liangzhou, sent his registrar Zong Chang as envoy.

sentences.zh: 敞父燮，呂光時自湟河太守入為尚書郎，見傉檀于廣武，執其手曰：「君神爽宏拔，逸氣陵雲，命世之傑也，必當克清世難。

translations.literal: Chang's father Xie, in Lü Guang's time, had entered the capital from Governor of Huanghe as Master of Writing; he met Rutan at Guangwu, took his hand, and said, "Lord, your spirit is lofty and sweeping, your free air towers over clouds—you are a hero of the age and will surely clear the world's troubles."
translations.idiomatic: Chang's father Xie had been governor of Huanghe under Lü Guang and later master of writing; meeting Rutan at Guangwu he took his hand and said, "You have the air of a hero of the age—you will clear the world's troubles."

sentences.zh: 恨吾年老不及見耳，以敞兄弟托君。

translations.literal: I regret my old age and cannot live to see it; I entrust Chang and his brothers to you."
translations.idiomatic: "I am too old to see it; I leave my sons to you."

sentences.zh: 」至是，傉檀謂敞曰：「孤以常才，謬為尊先君所見稱，每自恐有累大人水鏡之明。

translations.literal: Now Rutan said to Chang, "With my ordinary talent I was wrongly praised by your late father; I always feared I would stain the great man's mirror-like clarity."
translations.idiomatic: Rutan told Chang, "Your father praised my small talent; I feared I would shame his judgment."

sentences.zh: 及忝家業，竊有懷君子。

translations.literal: When I shamefully inherited the family enterprise, I secretly cherished the gentleman's regard.
translations.idiomatic: "When I took the realm I still held his kindness in my heart."

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：'中心藏之，何日忘之。

translations.literal: The Odes say, 'Hidden in the center—what day shall I forget it.'
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, 'Kept in the heart—when shall I forget?'

sentences.zh: '不圖今日得見卿也。

translations.literal: "I never thought that today I would see you."
translations.idiomatic: "I never thought to see you today."

sentences.zh: 」敞曰：「大王仁侔魏祖，存念先人，雖硃暉眄張堪之孤，叔向撫汝齊之子，無以加也。

translations.literal: Chang said, "Great king, your benevolence matches Wei Zu; in remembering my forebear, though Zhu Hui looked on Zhang Kan's orphan and Shu Xiang raised Qi Zi's son, they could add nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "Your kindness matches Cao Cao's; in honoring my father you surpass even the famous kindnesses of old."

sentences.zh: 」酒酣，語及平生。

translations.literal: When the wine was deep they spoke of their whole lives.
translations.idiomatic: Over wine they spoke of their lives.

sentences.zh: 傉檀曰：「卿魯子敬之儔，恨不與卿共成大業耳。」

translations.literal: Rutan said, "You are Lu Su's equal—I regret not sharing the great enterprise with you."
translations.idiomatic: Rutan said, "You are Lu Su's peer—I regret we did not build the realm together."

sentences.zh: 傉檀以姚興之盛，又密圖姑臧，乃去其年號，罷尚書丞郎官，遣參軍關尚聘於興。

translations.literal: Because Yao Xing was strong and Rutan secretly plotted Guzang, he abolished his era name, dismissed Masters of Writing and attendants, and sent Staff Officer Guan Shang as envoy to Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Yao Xing's power and plotting Guzang, Rutan dropped his era title, cut court offices, and sent Guan Shang to Xing.

sentences.zh: 興謂尚曰：「車騎投誠獻款，為國籓屏，擅興兵眾，輒造大城，為臣之道固若是乎？

translations.literal: Xing said to Shang, "The chariot commander offers sincerity and tribute as the state's frontier shield, yet on his own he raises troops and builds a great city—is this how a minister should act?"
translations.idiomatic: Xing asked Shang, "Your lord submits as a frontier shield, yet raises troops and builds a great city—is that how a vassal behaves?"

sentences.zh: 」尚曰：「王侯設險以自固，先王之制也，所以安人衛眾，預備不虞。

translations.literal: Shang said, "Lords and marquises set defenses to secure themselves—this is the former kings' institution, to settle the people and guard the host and prepare against the unforeseen."
translations.idiomatic: Shang said, "Princes fortify themselves by ancient rule—to guard their people and meet sudden danger."

sentences.zh: 車騎僻在遐籓，密邇勍寇，南則逆羌未賓，西則蒙遜跋扈，蓋為國家重門之防，不圖陛下忽以為嫌。

translations.literal: The chariot commander is remote on the frontier, close to fierce foes; south the rebellious Qiang are not yet submitted, west Mengxun is overbearing—it is a double gate for the state; we did not think Your Majesty would suddenly take offense."
translations.idiomatic: "Your servant sits on the frontier beside strong enemies—Qiang unrest in the south, Mengxun proud in the west. The walls are the realm's outer gate; we did not think you would take offense."

sentences.zh: 」興笑曰：「卿言是也。」

translations.literal: Xing laughed and said, "Your words are right."
translations.idiomatic: Xing laughed and said, "Well spoken."

sentences.zh: 傉檀遣其將文支討南羌、西虜，大破之。

translations.literal: Rutan sent his general Wenzhi to campaign against the southern Qiang and western barbarians and broke them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan sent Wenzhi against the southern Qiang and western tribes and routed them.

sentences.zh: 上表姚興，求涼州，不許，加傉檀散騎常侍，增邑二千戶。

translations.literal: He memorialized Yao Xing requesting Liangzhou; it was not granted, but Rutan was made Regular Attendant with an added fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He asked Xing for Liangzhou and was refused, but was made Regular Attendant with two thousand added households.

sentences.zh: 傉檀於是率師伐沮渠蒙遜，次於氐池。

translations.literal: Rutan thereupon led troops against Juqu Mengxun and encamped at Dichi.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan then marched on Juqu Mengxun and camped at Dichi.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜嬰城固守，芟其禾苗，至於赤泉而還。

translations.literal: Mengxun held the city fast; they cut his grain and millet and returned as far as Chiquan.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun held his walls; they ravaged his crops and withdrew to Chiquan.

sentences.zh: 獻興馬三千匹，羊三萬頭。

translations.literal: He presented Xing with three thousand horses and thirty thousand sheep.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Xing three thousand horses and thirty thousand sheep.

sentences.zh: 興乃署傉檀為使持節、都督河右諸軍事、車騎大將軍、領護匈奴中郎將、涼州刺史，常侍、公如故，鎮姑臧。

translations.literal: Xing then appointed Rutan Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all military affairs in Hexi, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Colonel Protector of the Xiongnu, Governor of Liangzhou, Regular Attendant and Duke as before, stationed at Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Xing then named Rutan commander of Hexi, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, protector of the Xiongnu, governor of Liangzhou, and duke as before, with his seat at Guzang.

sentences.zh: 傉檀率步騎三萬次於五澗，興涼州刺史王尚遣辛晁、孟禕、彭敏出迎。

translations.literal: Rutan led thirty thousand foot and horse to encamp at Wujian; Wang Shang, Xing's inspector of Liangzhou, sent Xin Chao, Meng Yi, and Peng Min out to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan led thirty thousand men to Wujian; Wang Shang sent Xin Chao, Meng Yi, and Peng Min to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 尚出自清陽門，鎮南文支入自涼風門。

translations.literal: Shang went out from the Clear Yang Gate; the south-pacifying commander Wenzhi entered from the Cool Wind Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Shang went out by the Clear Yang Gate; Wenzhi entered by the Cool Wind Gate.

sentences.zh: 宗敞以別駕送尚還長安，傉檀曰：「吾得涼州三千餘家，情之所寄，唯卿一人，奈何舍我去乎？

translations.literal: Zong Chang as vice director escorted Shang back to Chang'an; Rutan said, "I have gained more than three thousand households of Liangzhou whom my heart trusts—you alone, how can you leave me?"
translations.idiomatic: Zong Chang escorted Shang to Chang'an; Rutan said, "I have won three thousand Liang households I lean on—you above all—how can you leave?"

sentences.zh: 」敞曰：「今送舊君，所以忠於殿下。

translations.literal: Chang said, "Now I escort the old lord—that is loyalty to your highness."
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "I serve the old master—that is loyalty to you."

sentences.zh: 」傉檀曰：「吾今新牧貴州，懷遠安邇之略，為之若何？

translations.literal: Rutan said, "I am newly governing this noble province—what policy wins the distant and settles the near?"
translations.idiomatic: Rutan asked, "I am new to this province—how shall I win the distant and settle the near?"

sentences.zh: 」敞曰：「涼土雖弊，形勝之地，道由人弘，實在殿下。

translations.literal: Chang said, "Though Liang soil is worn, it is ground of strategic advantage; the Way is advanced by men—it lies with your highness."
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "Liang is weary but strong in position; men make the Way—it rests with you."

sentences.zh: 段懿、孟禕、武威之宿望；

translations.literal: Duan Yi and Meng Yi are longstanding hopes of Wuwei;
translations.idiomatic: Duan Yi and Meng Yi are the old pillars of Wuwei;

sentences.zh: 辛晁、彭敏，秦、隴之冠冕；

translations.literal: Xin Chao and Peng Min—the crown and cap of Qin and Long;
translations.idiomatic: Xin Chao and Peng Min stand foremost among the gentry of Qin and Longyou.

sentences.zh: 斐敏、馬輔，中州之令族；

translations.literal: Fei Min and Ma Fu—leading clans of the central provinces;
translations.idiomatic: Fei Min and Ma Fu head eminent families of the heartland.

sentences.zh: 張昶，涼國之舊胤；

translations.literal: Zhang Chang—a scion of the old Liang royal house;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang carries the blood of the former Liang kings.

sentences.zh: 張穆、邊憲、文齊、楊班、梁崧、趙昌，武同飛、羽。

translations.literal: Zhang Mu, Bian Xian, Wen Qi, Yang Ban, Liang Song, and Zhao Chang—in martial valor they match Flying and Feathered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mu, Bian Xian, Wen Qi, Yang Ban, Liang Song, and Zhao Chang fight with the renown of Li Guang and Huo Qubing.

sentences.zh: 以大王之神略，撫之以威信，農戰並修，文教兼設，可以從橫於天下，河右豈足定乎！

translations.literal: With Your Highness's divine strategy, governing them with prestige and faith, cultivating both agriculture and war, setting up both civil and military teaching—you could league and counter-league across the empire; how could the lands west of the River alone suffice as your limit!
translations.idiomatic: Under your genius, rule them with awe and good faith; train the fields and the ranks alike, and pair arms with letters—you could play the great powers against one another under heaven. Why should the Hexi corridor be the end of your ambition?

sentences.zh: 」傉檀大悅，賜敞馬二十匹。

translations.literal: Rutan was greatly pleased and granted Zong Chang twenty horses.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan was delighted and gave Zong Chang twenty horses.

sentences.zh: 於是大饗文武于謙光殿，班賜金馬各有差。

translations.literal: Thereupon he held a great feast for civil and military officials in the Hall of Modest Radiance, distributing gifts of gold and horses in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: He then feasted his civil and military officers in the Hall of Modest Radiance, awarding gold and horses in graded shares.

sentences.zh: 遣西曹從事史暠聘于姚興。

translations.literal: He sent Western Bureau Attendant Shi Hao as envoy to pay a courtesy visit to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Shi Hao of the Western Bureau as envoy to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 興謂暠曰：「車騎坐定涼州，衣錦本國，其德我乎？

translations.literal: Xing said to Hao: "The General of Chariots and Cavalry has settled Liangzhou and returned in brocade to his native state—does he owe me gratitude?"
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing asked Hao, "The Chariots-and-Cavalry General has secured Liangzhou and come home in glory—does he feel beholden to me?"

sentences.zh: 」暠曰：「車騎積德河西，少播英問，王威未接，投誠萬里，陛下官方任才，量功授職，彝倫之常，何德之有！

translations.literal: Hao replied: "The General amassed merit west of the He, but little spread his fine renown; Your Majesty's royal majesty had not yet reached him, and he pledged loyalty from ten thousand li away. Your Majesty appoints talent to office and grants posts according to merit—the constant norms of order; what debt of gratitude is there!"
translations.idiomatic: Hao answered, "The General built his name in Hexi and offered allegiance from afar before your majesty's writ had reached him. You place men by merit and office by measure—that is the way of kings. What debt is there?"

sentences.zh: 」興曰：「朕不以州授車騎者，車騎何從得之。

translations.literal: Xing said: "Had I not granted the province to the General, how would he have obtained it?"
translations.idiomatic: Xing said, "If I had not given him the province, how would he have gained it?"

sentences.zh: 」暠曰：「使河西雲擾、呂氏顛狽者，實由車騎兄弟傾其根本。

translations.literal: Hao said: "That Hexi was clouded with turmoil and the Lü house overthrown—this was truly because the General and his brothers overturned their foundation."
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "The storms in Hexi and the fall of the Lü were wrought by the General and his brothers uprooting their rule."

sentences.zh: 陛下雖鴻羅遐被，涼州猶在天網之外。

translations.literal: Your Majesty though your great net spreads to distant lands, Liangzhou remained outside Heaven's mesh.
translations.idiomatic: Though your reach extends far, Liangzhou still lay beyond your net.

sentences.zh: 故征西以周、召之重，力屈姑臧；

translations.literal: Hence the Campaigning West General, with the weight of the Zhou dukes of Zhou and Shao, had his strength broken at Guzang;
translations.idiomatic: So the Campaigning West General, burdened like the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao, was spent before Guzang;

sentences.zh: 齊難以王旅之盛，勢挫張掖。

translations.literal: Qi Nan with the splendor of the royal host had his momentum checked at Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: and Qi Nan, at the head of the imperial host, was turned back at Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 王尚孤城獨守，外逼群狄，陛下不連兵十年，殫竭中國，涼州未易取也。

translations.literal: Wang Shang held a lone city in isolation, pressed from without by hordes of barbarians; unless Your Majesty campaigned in force for ten years and exhausted the Middle Kingdom, Liangzhou would not be easily taken.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shang held one city alone against surrounding tribes. Without ten years of war and the draining of the realm, Liangzhou would not have been easily won.

sentences.zh: 今以虛名假人，內收大利，乃知妙算自天，聖與道合，雖云遷授，蓋亦時宜。

translations.literal: Now by lending an empty title you gain within a great profit—thus one knows subtle calculation comes from Heaven and the Sage accords with the Way; though it is called a transfer of appointment, it is surely timely.
translations.idiomatic: Now you grant a hollow title and reap a rich gain within—proof that Heaven aids your reckoning and the sage-king moves with the Way. Though men call it a transfer of office, it is simply what the hour demands.

sentences.zh: 」興悅其言，拜騎都尉。

translations.literal: Xing was pleased with his words and appointed him Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Pleased with his reply, Xing made him Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 傉檀宴群僚於宣德堂，仰視而歎曰：「古人言作者不居，居者不作，信矣。

translations.literal: Rutan feasted his officials in the Hall of Illustrious Virtue and, looking up, sighed: "The ancients said 'he who builds does not dwell in it; he who dwells in it does not build'—how true!"
translations.idiomatic: Rutan entertained his ministers in the Hall of Illustrious Virtue, gazed upward, and sighed, "The ancients were right: those who build do not long enjoy; those who enjoy did not build."

sentences.zh: 」孟禕進曰：「張文王築城苑，繕宗廟，為貽厥之資，萬世之業，秦師濟河，漼然瓦解。

translations.literal: Meng Yi advanced and said: "Prince Zhang Wen of Former Liang built walls and parks and repaired ancestral temples as resources to pass down and an enterprise for ten thousand generations—yet when Qin troops crossed the river, it dissolved streaming away."
translations.idiomatic: Meng Yi spoke up: "Prince Zhang Wen raised walls and gardens and restored the ancestral shrines for heirs yet unborn—yet when Qin armies crossed the river, his house melted away like ice in sun."

sentences.zh: 梁熙據全州之地，擁十萬之眾，軍敗於酒泉，身死于彭濟。

translations.literal: Liang Xi held the territory of the whole province and commanded a host of a hundred thousand; his army was defeated at Jiuquan and he himself died at Pengji.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Xi held the whole province and a hundred thousand men, yet lost his army at Jiuquan and his life at Pengji.

sentences.zh: 呂氏以排山之勢，王有西夏，率土崩離，銜璧秦、雍。

translations.literal: The Lü house with momentum to topple mountains ruled the Western Xia, yet the realm collapsed and they came bearing jade to Qin and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: The Lü, who seemed able to overturn mountains and ruled Western Xia, saw their lands crumble until they surrendered with jade seals to Qin and Yong.

sentences.zh: 寬饒有言：'富貴無常，忽輒易人。

translations.literal: Kuang Rao had a saying: 'Wealth and rank have no constancy; suddenly they pass to another.'
translations.idiomatic: Kuang Rao once said, "Fortune and office never stay fixed; in a blink they change hands."

sentences.zh: '此堂之建，年垂百載，十有二主，唯信順可以久安，仁義可以永固，願大王勉之。

translations.literal: This hall has stood nearly a hundred years and known twelve lords; only trust and obedience can long preserve, and benevolence and righteousness can eternally secure—may Your Highness exert yourself therein.
translations.idiomatic: This hall is nearly a century old and has seen twelve masters. Only loyalty and compliance keep a house long; only benevolence and right keep it firm. I urge Your Highness to live by that.

sentences.zh: 」傉檀曰：「非君無以聞讜言也。

translations.literal: Rutan said: "Without you I would not have heard such upright counsel."
translations.idiomatic: Rutan said, "Without you I would never have heard such honest counsel."

sentences.zh: 」傉檀雖受制于姚興，然車服禮章一如王者。

translations.literal: Though Rutan was subject to Yao Xing, his chariots, robes, and ritual regalia were entirely like a king's.
translations.idiomatic: Though he owed allegiance to Yao Xing, Rutan's carriages, dress, and court ritual matched a king's.

sentences.zh: 以宗敞為太府主簿、錄記室事。

translations.literal: He appointed Zong Chang Registrar of the Grand Treasury and Recorder of Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He made Zong Chang Registrar of the Grand Treasury and chief recorder of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 傉檀偽遊澆河，襲徙西平、湟河諸羌三萬餘戶于武興、番禾、武威、昌松四郡。

translations.literal: Rutan feigned a tour of the Jiao River and surreptitiously moved more than thirty thousand households of the various Qiang of Xiping and Huangshui to the four commanderies of Wuxing, Fanhe, Wuwei, and Changsong.
translations.idiomatic: Pretending a pleasure tour along the Jiao River, Rutan secretly relocated more than thirty thousand Qiang households from Xiping and Huangshui into Wuxing, Fanhe, Wuwei, and Changsong.

sentences.zh: 徵集戎夏之兵五萬餘人，大閱于方亭，遂伐沮渠蒙遜，入西陝。

translations.literal: He mustered more than fifty thousand troops of both barbarian and Chinese arms, held a grand review at Fangting, and then marched against Juqu Mengxun, entering Western Shaan.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered over fifty thousand barbarian and Chinese troops, reviewed them at Fangting, and marched against Juqu Mengxun into western Shaan.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜率眾來距，戰于均石，為蒙遜所敗。

translations.literal: Mengxun led his forces to oppose him; they fought at Junshi and Rutan was defeated by Mengxun.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun came out to meet him; at Junshi Rutan was beaten.

sentences.zh: 傉檀率騎二萬，運谷四萬石以給西郡。

translations.literal: Rutan led twenty thousand horse and transported forty thousand piculs of grain to supply Western Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan led twenty thousand cavalry and hauled forty thousand piculs of grain to provision Western Commandery.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜攻西郡，陷之。

translations.literal: Mengxun attacked Western Commandery and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun assaulted Western Commandery and captured it.

sentences.zh: 其後傉檀又與赫連勃勃戰于陽武，為勃勃所敗，將佐死者十餘人，傉檀與數騎奔南山，幾為追騎所得。

translations.literal: Afterward Rutan again fought Helian Bobo at Yangwu and was beaten by Bobo; more than ten of his officers and aides died. Rutan fled south into the mountains with a few horse and was nearly caught by pursuing riders.
translations.idiomatic: Later Rutan fought Helian Bobo at Yangwu and lost again; a dozen officers fell. He escaped into the southern hills with only a few riders and was almost overtaken.

sentences.zh: 傉檀懼東西寇至，徙三百里內百姓入于姑臧，國中駭怨。

translations.literal: Rutan, fearing enemies from east and west, moved the populace within three hundred li into Guzang; the realm was stricken with alarm and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing attack from both quarters, Rutan moved everyone within three hundred li into Guzang, and the whole state groaned in fear and anger.

sentences.zh: 屠各成七兒因百姓之擾也，率其屬三百人，叛傉檀於北城。

translations.literal: The Tufa Cheng Qi'er, taking advantage of the people's distress, led three hundred of his followers in rebellion against Rutan at the North City.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Qi'er of the Tufa, exploiting the people's turmoil, led three hundred men in revolt at the North City.

sentences.zh: 推梁貴為盟主，貴閉門不應。

translations.literal: They tried to make Liang Gui covenant chief, but Gui shut his door and would not respond.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed Liang Gui to lead them, but he barred his gate and refused.

sentences.zh: 一夜眾至數千。

translations.literal: In one night the mob grew to several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: By morning their numbers had swelled to several thousand.

sentences.zh: 殿中都尉張猛大言於眾曰：「主上陽武之敗，蓋恃眾故也。

translations.literal: Palace Interior Commandant Zhang Meng addressed the crowd loudly: "Our lord's defeat at Yangwu was surely because he relied on numbers."
translations.idiomatic: Palace Commandant Zhang Meng cried to the throng, "Our lord's loss at Yangwu came of trusting too many men."

sentences.zh: 責躬悔過，明君之義，諸君何故從此小人作不義之事！

translations.literal: To blame oneself and repent is the duty of an enlightened ruler—why do you gentlemen follow this petty man in an unrighteous deed!
translations.idiomatic: A wise ruler blames himself and mends his ways—why follow this nobody into treason?

sentences.zh: 殿內武旅正爾相尋，目前之危，悔將無及。

translations.literal: The palace guard is even now closing in; the peril before your eyes—regret will come too late.
translations.idiomatic: The palace guard is already on you. Disaster is at hand; repent now or never.

sentences.zh: 」眾聞之，咸散。

translations.literal: When the crowd heard this, all dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: At his words the mob melted away.

sentences.zh: 七兒奔晏然，殿中騎將白路等追斬之。

translations.literal: Qi'er fled to Yanran; Palace Cavalry General Bai Lu and others pursued and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Qi'er fled to Yanran; Bai Lu, palace cavalry commander, overtook and killed him.

sentences.zh: 軍諮祭酒梁裒、輔國司馬邊憲等七人謀反，傉檀悉誅之。

translations.literal: Military Adviser Sacrificial Officer Liang Pou, Assisting State Major Bian Xian, and seven others plotted rebellion; Rutan executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Pou, military adviser, Bian Xian, assisting-state major, and five others plotted revolt; Rutan put them all to death.

sentences.zh: 姚興以傉檀外有陽武之敗，內有邊、梁之亂，遣其尚書郎韋宗來觀釁。

translations.literal: Yao Xing, because Rutan had without the Yangwu defeat and within the Bian and Liang troubles, sent his Master of Writing Wei Zong to observe whether there was an opening.
translations.idiomatic: With Yangwu lost without and the Bian and Liang plots within, Yao Xing sent Master of Writing Wei Zong to probe for weakness.

sentences.zh: 傉檀與宗論六國從橫之規，三家戰爭之略，遠言天命廢興，近陳人事成敗，機變無窮，辭致清辯。

translations.literal: Rutan debated with Zong the schemes of the Six States' alliances and the strategies of the Three Kingdoms' wars, speaking from afar on the rise and fall ordained by Heaven and from near on success and failure in human affairs—infinite in resource, his rhetoric lucid and keen.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan discoursed with him on Warring States alliances and Three Kingdoms stratagems, on Heaven's mandate in the distance and men's fortunes close at hand—endlessly inventive, his speech bright and sharp.

sentences.zh: 宗出而歎曰：「命世大才、經綸名教者，不必華宗夏士；

translations.literal: Zong left and sighed: "A generation-defining great talent who orders civilization through the classics need not be from a splendid clan or Xia gentry;"
translations.idiomatic: Leaving, Zong sighed, "A man who shapes an age and orders the rites need not spring from a noble house or Han stock;"

sentences.zh: 撥煩理亂、澄氣濟世者，亦未必《八索》、《九丘》。

translations.literal: one who clears troubles, settles chaos, clarifies the spirit, and aids the age need not have studied the Eight Canons or Nine Mounds.
translations.idiomatic: nor need one who cuts through disorder and steadies the realm have read the Eight Canons or Nine Mounds.

sentences.zh: 五經之外，冠冕之表，復自有人。

translations.literal: Beyond the Five Classics, atop the crown of excellence, there are again men of their own kind.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the Five Classics, among the foremost of the land, others still arise.

sentences.zh: 車騎神機秀髮，信一代之偉人，由余、日磾豈足為多也！

translations.literal: The General is divine in counsel and splendid in gifts—truly a great man of an age; You Yu and Lil Wenzhen are hardly worth counting!
translations.idiomatic: The Chariots-and-Cavalry General is keen-witted and brilliant—a true giant of his time. You Yu and Jinti are nothing beside him!

sentences.zh: 」宗還長安，言於興曰：「涼州雖殘弊之後，風化未頹，傉檀權詐多方，憑山河之固，未可圖也。

translations.literal: Zong returned to Chang'an and said to Xing: "Though Liangzhou is in the aftermath of ruin, its customs have not yet collapsed. Rutan is resourceful in many stratagems and leans on the strength of mountains and rivers—it cannot yet be plotted against."
translations.idiomatic: Back in Chang'an, Zong told Xing, "Liangzhou is battered but not broken. Rutan is cunning and holds the mountains and rivers—do not think him easy prey."

sentences.zh: 」興曰：「勃勃以烏合之眾尚能破之，吾以天下之兵，何足克也！

translations.literal: Xing said: "Bobo with a mob still broke him—how could he stand against me with the armies of the empire!"
translations.idiomatic: Xing said, "Bobo with a rabble beat him. With the armies of the realm, how can I fail?"

sentences.zh: 」宗曰：「形移勢變，終始殊途，陵人者易敗，自守者難攻。

translations.literal: Zong said: "Forms shift and momentum changes; beginning and end follow different paths. He who bullies others is easily defeated; he who holds himself is hard to assault."
translations.idiomatic: Zong said, "Situations turn; what worked once fails next. The aggressor breaks easily; the defender is hard to crack."

sentences.zh: 陽武之役，傉檀以輕勃勃致敗。

translations.literal: At Yangwu Rutan underestimated Bobo and met defeat.
translations.idiomatic: At Yangwu Rutan slighted Bobo and lost.

sentences.zh: 今以大軍臨之，必自固求全，臣竊料群臣無傉檀匹也。

translations.literal: Now with a great army bearing down, he will surely fortify himself and seek preservation; I privately judge none of his ministers can match Rutan.
translations.idiomatic: If a great host comes now, he will dig in and save himself—and I doubt any of his ministers equal Rutan.

sentences.zh: 雖以天威臨之，未見其利。

translations.literal: Even with Heaven's majesty pressing upon him, I see no profit in it.
translations.idiomatic: Even with imperial might against him, I see little gain.

sentences.zh: 」興不從，乃遣其將姚弼及斂成等率步騎三萬來伐，又使其將姚顯為弼等後繼，遺傉檀書云「遣尚書左僕射齊難討勃勃，懼其西逸，故令弼等於河西邀之。

translations.literal: Xing would not heed him and sent his generals Yao Bi and Qincheng at the head of thirty thousand foot and horse to attack, also sending his general Yao Xian to follow Bi as rear guard. He sent Rutan a letter saying: "I have dispatched Minister of the Left Qi Nan to punish Bobo, fearing he might flee west—therefore I have Bi and others intercept him in Hexi."
translations.idiomatic: Xing refused and sent Yao Bi and Qincheng with thirty thousand foot and horse to invade, with Yao Xian following as reserve. He wrote Rutan: "I have sent Qi Nan, Minister of the Left, against Bobo and fear he may slip west—Bi is posted in Hexi to block him."

sentences.zh: 」傉檀以為然，遂不設備。

translations.literal: Rutan believed it and therefore made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan took the letter at face value and left his guard down.

sentences.zh: 弼眾至漠口，昌松太守蘇霸嬰城固守，弼喻霸令降，霸曰：「汝違負盟誓，伐委順之籓，天地有靈，將不祐汝！

translations.literal: Bi's host reached Mokou; Changsong Administrator Su Ba barred the gates and held firm. Bi urged Ba to surrender. Ba said: "You have broken your sworn oath and attack a submissive frontier state—Heaven and Earth have spirit; they will not bless you!"
translations.idiomatic: Bi reached Mokou; Su Ba, Changsong's governor, shut the walls. Bi called on him to yield. Ba replied, "You broke your oath and strike a loyal frontier—Heaven and Earth see; they will not aid you!"

sentences.zh: 吾甯為涼鬼，何降之有！

translations.literal: I would rather be a Liang ghost—why should I surrender!
translations.idiomatic: I would sooner be a ghost of Liang than submit—never!

sentences.zh: 」城陷，斬霸。

translations.literal: The city fell and Ba was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell; Su Ba was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 弼至姑臧，屯於西苑。

translations.literal: Bi reached Guzang and encamped in the Western Park.
translations.idiomatic: Bi came to Guzang and camped in the Western Park.

sentences.zh: 州人王鐘、宋鐘、王娥等密為內應，候人執其使送之。

translations.literal: Prefecture natives Wang Zhong, Song Zhong, Wang E, and others secretly served as inside collaborators; scouts seized their messenger and delivered him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhong, Song Zhong, Wang E, and others of the province plotted treason within; scouts caught their courier and brought him in.

sentences.zh: 傉檀欲誅其元首，前軍伊力延侯曰：「今強敵在外，內有奸豎，兵交勢踧，禍難不輕，宜悉坑之以安內外。

translations.literal: Rutan wished to execute the ringleaders; Vanguard General Yiliyanhou said: "Now with a strong foe outside and traitors within, armies clashing and momentum cramped—calamity is no light matter. All should be thrown into pits to secure within and without."
translations.idiomatic: Rutan meant to kill the leaders; vanguard general Yiliyanhou said, "With the enemy outside and traitors inside, battle pressing and peril near, the danger is grave. Exterminate them all to steady within and without."

sentences.zh: 」傉檀從之，殺五千餘人，以婦女為軍賞。

translations.literal: Rutan followed this, killing more than five thousand, and took the women as military rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan agreed, slaughtered more than five thousand, and gave the women to the troops as booty.

sentences.zh: 命諸郡縣悉驅牛羊於野，斂成縱兵虜掠。

translations.literal: He ordered all commanderies and districts to drive cattle and sheep into the open country; Qincheng let his troops loose to plunder captives.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered every district to drive herds into the open; Qincheng's men swept the countryside for plunder.

sentences.zh: 傉檀遣其鎮北俱延、鎮軍敬歸等十將率騎分擊，大敗之，斬首七千餘級。
